sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: GPT-SoVITS is a text-to-speech and voice conversion tool with a web interface. From a 5-second voice sample it can speak new text in that voice, and fine-tuning on about 1 minute of audio makes the voice more similar and realistic.
sixtySeconds.problem: Training a custom text-to-speech voice usually needs hours of recordings. GPT-SoVITS works from seconds to a minute of audio and bundles tools for preparing training data, so beginners can build voice models.
whoFor: Developers experimenting with custom TTS voices
Hobbyists working with Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Cantonese or English speech
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for strong few-shot voice cloning with a WebUI and built-in dataset tools. Windows users can download an integrated package and skip the setup.
requirements: NVIDIA CUDA, Apple silicon or CPU

overview: GPT-SoVITS supports zero-shot TTS from a 5-second sample and few-shot fine-tuning with 1 minute of data. It can speak in a language different from the training data, currently English, Japanese, Korean, Cantonese and Chinese.

The WebUI includes tools for separating vocals from accompaniment, slicing audio into training chunks, Chinese speech recognition and text labelling. A fine-tuning tab walks you from audio path to slicing, denoising, ASR, proofreading and training, and a separate inference tab generates speech.

The README reports an inference real-time factor of 0.028 on an RTX 4060 Ti and 0.014 on an RTX 4090 for the v2 ProPlus model. On Macs, models trained on GPU have significantly lower quality, so the project uses CPU there for now. It is MIT licensed.

steps.title: Download the integrated package
steps.body: Download the package linked in the README (Windows 10 or newer), extract it and double-click go-webui.bat.

steps.title: Create a conda environment
steps.code:
conda create -n GPTSoVits python=3.10
conda activate GPTSoVits

steps.title: Run the installer
steps.body: --device is CU126, CU128, ROCM or CPU; --source is HF, HF-Mirror or ModelScope. Add --download-uvr5 for the vocal separation models.
